source.title: How Much Over-parameterization Is Sufficient to Learn Deep ReLU Networks?
source.authors: Zixiang Chen; Yuan Cao; Difan Zou; Quanquan Gu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and experiments.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports an experiment measuring the minimum width needed for gradient descent to achieve zero training error, using fully connected networks on binary CIFAR-10 subsets. This is a different model and setting from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The experiment reports minimum width by sample size for two binary CIFAR-10 class pairs. Width values are shown only in Figure 1; the text describes the outcome as polylogarithmic. Theoretical convergence and generalization guarantees are not empirical results on classification-error rates, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional convergence guarantees and reports zero-error width thresholds for fully connected ReLU networks on binary CIFAR-10 subsets. V1 specifies convolutional networks; V2 specifies teacher-student spurious minima. Neither the experiment nor the theory tests those versions, and no results compare initialization, shortcuts, stability thresholds, or batch normalization for V3–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate with its assumption qualifier. The authors establish conditional optimization and generalization guarantees for fully connected deep ReLU binary classifiers, with polylogarithmic width under suitable separability assumptions. They interpret the two binary CIFAR-10 experiments as consistent with that scaling; the finite plots do not establish an asymptotic growth law.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical experiment uses a 5-layer fully connected ReLU network on two binary CIFAR-10 subsets; the paper's theory analyzes GD and SGD with Gaussian random initialization and cross-entropy loss. The experiment description does not state the optimizer or training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Training sample size and binary CIFAR-10 class pair vary; Figure 1 plots four polylogarithmic reference curves.

fits_no_version.finding: Section D reports minimum widths achieving zero training error for a five-layer fully connected ReLU network on cat-versus-dog and cat-versus-ship CIFAR-10 subsets, at seven sample sizes from 100 to 10,000. The authors characterize the plotted growth as polylogarithmic; numerical width values are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Five-layer fully connected ReLU networks can fit these binary CIFAR-10 subsets, with required width reported to grow polylogarithmically over the tested sample sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 3.3 bounds GD training loss by three times the best NTRF reference loss. Under suitable separation assumptions, polylogarithmic width suffices; Section 4.3 instead requires polynomial width under class-dependent nondegeneration, which covers random labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Randomly initialized fully connected deep ReLU networks have conditional convergence guarantees whose sufficient width depends on data separability.

record.problems: The reported experiment covers only a two-class subset of CIFAR-10 and a 5-layer fully connected network; optimizer and detailed training recipe are not stated in the experiment description. Figure 1 values are not available as text.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels and the stated smaller-model, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, frequencies of spurious local minima, and adding one or two student neurons relative to teacher width.
Training-error degradation across depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the special initialization exceptions.
Comparative effects of initialization on signal propagation, learning speed, and trainable depth. Using He initialization in the theory does not test its advantage.
Recovery, divergence, and curvature trajectories relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The cannot_determine states concern applicability to the listed versions and unreadable width values; they do not dispute the text's report that selected networks achieved zero training error.

versions.untested_parts: The experiment uses fully connected networks on binary CIFAR-10 subsets, not convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100; it does not report corrupted or random labels, smaller-model failures, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
No teacher-student local-minima comparison or student-width sweep relative to teacher width.
No comparison of plain and residual networks across depth.
No comparison of initializations or trainable depth under different initializations.
No above-stability learning-rate experiment or curvature measurement.
